correctness.rationale: Ambient point separation makes the restriction field \(K_C\) a point-separating intermediate field \(\mathbb C(u)\subset K_C\subset\mathcal M(C)\) with finite upper extension. The compact-curve function-field correspondence gives a finite map of degree \([\mathcal M(C):K_C]\); point separation forces that degree to be one. Field generation then lifts to genuine ambient meromorphic extension by using the same finite rational expression. The Picard consequence follows from restricting an effective meromorphic fiber divisor to the curve.
